subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw implement native per-agent spend-budget enforcement in core, expose a budget-capable plugin/admission API, or leave enforcement to ClawRouter/external/provider controls?
rationale: The remaining work sets new config, provider dispatch policy, persistent accounting state, fallback behavior, and operator UX, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Native core admission layer
options.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets as a core pre-dispatch path with durable SQLite accounting, reservations/refunds, receipts, status/doctor surfaces, and plugin observability hooks.

options.title: Plugin/API-first boundary
options.body: Extend the plugin/admission contract enough for external budget systems to enforce before dispatch while keeping core limited to generic hooks and reporting.

options.title: External controls only
options.body: Defer native enforcement and document ClawRouter, provider accounts, balances, quotas, and local proxies as the supported budget-control path.

recommendation.title: Native core admission layer
recommendation.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets as a core pre-dispatch path with durable SQLite accounting, reservations/refunds, receipts, status/doctor surfaces, and plugin observability hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest observed connection to adjacent cost reporting, ClawRouter quota work, and prior product-boundary decisions for cost-observer scope.
